<transformation>
The input is treated as a tile map. The output is NxM times larger than the input (where the input is N rows x M cols). Each input cell at (BR, BC) with a non-zero value causes a copy of the full input to be placed in the corresponding NxM block of the output (at rows BR*N .. BR*N+N-1, cols BC*M .. BC*M+M-1). Each input cell with value 0 produces an all-zero block at that position.
</transformation>

<asp>
% Count distinct row/col indices — equals grid dimensions for 0-indexed inputs
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Output is NR*NR rows and NC*NC cols (input tiled by itself)
output_cell(R, C) :-
    input(BR, BC, _), input(DR, DC, _),
    n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
    R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC.

1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Non-zero block: the sub-cell must equal the input value at the relative position
:- input(BR, BC, V), V != 0,
   input(DR, DC, TileColor),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != TileColor.

% Zero block: every sub-cell must be 0
:- input(BR, BC, 0),
   input(DR, DC, _),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != 0.
</asp>
</example_1>

<transformation>
The output is the same size as the input. Color-3 cells are unchanged. Non-3 cells (value 0) that are enclosed by color-3 walls — i.e., cannot reach the grid boundary via 4-connected movement through non-3 cells — are filled with color 4. All other non-3 cells remain 0.
</transformation>

<asp>
% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- input(R, C, _).
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Grid boundary coordinates
min_row(R) :- R = #min{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
max_row(R) :- R = #max{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
min_col(C) :- C = #min{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.
max_col(C) :- C = #max{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.

% 4-connected adjacency offsets
delta(0,1). delta(0,-1). delta(1,0). delta(-1,0).

% Non-3 cells on the grid boundary are reachable from outside
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_row(Rmin), R = Rmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_row(Rmax), R = Rmax.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_col(Cmin), C = Cmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_col(Cmax), C = Cmax.

% Flood-fill outward through non-3 cells
outside(R2, C2) :-
    outside(R1, C1), delta(DR, DC),
    R2 = R1+DR, C2 = C1+DC,
    input(R2, C2, V), V != 3.

% Color-3 cells stay 3
:- input(R, C, 3), output(R, C, Color), Color != 3.

% Outside non-3 cells stay 0
:- outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 0.

% Interior non-3 cells (enclosed by 3s, not reachable from boundary) become 4
:- input(R, C, 0), not outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 4.
</asp>
</example_2>

% Define input and output facts are injected automatically.

% Determine rows and columns
max_row(Rmax) :- Rmax = #max{R : input(R,_,_)}.
max_col(Cmax) :- Cmax = #max{C : input(_,C,_)}.
n_rows(NR) :- NR = Rmax + 1.
n_cols(NC) :- NC = Cmax + 1.

% Wall cells (color 5)
wall(R,C) :- input(R,C,5).

% 4-neighbour offsets
delta(0,1). delta(0,-1). delta(1,0). delta(-1,0).

% Neighborhood (only through non-wall cells)
neighbor(R,C,R2,C2) :-
    delta(DR,DC),
    R2 = R + DR,
    C2 = C + DC,
    R2 >= 0,
    R2 < NR,
    C2 >= 0,
    C2 < NC,
    input(R2,C2,_),
    not wall(R2,C2).

% Reachability among non-wall cells
reachable(R,C,R,C).
reachable(R,C,R2,C2) :- neighbor(R,C,R2,C2).
reachable(R,C,R2,C2) :- reachable(R,C,R1,C1), neighbor(R1,C1,R2,C2).

% Check if there exists a larger value in the component
exists_higher(R,C,Max) :-
    Max1 = Max + 1,
    Max1 <= 9,
    reachable(R,C,R2,C2),
    input(R2,C2,V),
    V != 5,
    V >= Max1.

% Max value of the component (non-wall)
max_comp(R,C,Max) :-
    not wall(R,C),
    reachable(R,C,R2,C2),
    input(R2,C2,Max),
    Max != 5,
    not exists_higher(R,C,Max).

% Output rules
output(R,C,5) :- wall(R,C).
output(R,C,Out) :-
    not wall(R,C),
    max_comp(R,C,Max),
    Out = Max + 5,
    Out >= 5,
    Out <= 9.

% Every cell must be output
output_cell(R,C) :- input(R,C,_).

% Exactly one answer set, exactly one color per cell
1 { output(R,C,Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).

% Color domain
color(0..9).

output_cell(R, C) :- input(R, C, _).

outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_col(Cmax), C = Cmax.

%  Dimensions of the input (rows and columns)
% -----------------------------------------------------------------
NR = #count{R : input(R,_,_)}.      % number of rows (0 … NR‑1)

%  Walls – colour 5 are never traversed

wall(R,C) :- input(R,C,5).

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%  4‑neighbour offsets
% -----------------------------------------------------------------
delta(0,1). delta(0,-1). delta(1,0). delta(-1,0).

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%  Adjacent non‑wall cell (4‑connected)
% -----------------------------------------------------------------
neighbor(R1,C1,R2,C2) :-
    delta(DR,DC),
    R2 = R1 + DR,
    C2 = C1 + DC,
    R2 >= 0,            R2 < NR,
    C2 >= 0,            C2 < NC,
    input(R2,C2,_),
    not wall(R2,C2),
    input(R1,C1,_),
    not wall(R1,C1).

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%  4‑connected reachability (only through non‑wall cells)
% -----------------------------------------------------------------
reachable(R,C,R,C) :- true.                     % reflexive
reachable(R,C,R2,C2) :-
    neighbor(R,C,R1,C1),
    reachable(R1,C1,R2,C2).

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%  Reachable cell with a colour (must not be a wall)
% -----------------------------------------------------------------
reachable_colour(R,C,Col) :-
    reachable(R,C,R2,C2),
    input(R2,C2,Col),
    Col != 5.

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%  Existence of a strictly higher colour reachable in the component
% -----------------------------------------------------------------
exists_higher(R,C,Col) :-
    Col1 = Col + 1,
    Col1 <= 9,
    Col1 != 5,

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
max_comp(R,C,Max) :-
    not wall(R,C),                     % (R,C) is a non‑wall cell

    input(R2,C2,Max),
    Max != 5,
    not exists_higher(R,C,Max).

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%  Output rules
% -----------------------------------------------------------------
% walls stay colour 5
output(R,C,5) :- wall(R,C).

% non‑wall cells obtain (max of component + 5)
output(R,C,Out) :-
    not wall(R,C),
    max_comp(R,C,Max),
    Out = Max + 5,

output_cell(R,C) :- input(R,C,_).

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
1 { output(R,C,Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).

%  Colour domain
% -----------------------------------------------------------------
color(0..9).

The input is treated as a tile map. The output is NxM times larger than the input (where the input is N rows x M cols). Each input cell at (BR, BC) with a non-zero value causes a copy of the full input to be placed in the corresponding NxM block of the output (at rows BR*N .. BR*N+N-1, cols BC*M .. BC*M+M-1). n_cols(N) :- N = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Output is NR*NR rows and NC*NC cols (input tiled by itself)
output_cell(R, C) :-
    input(BR, BC, _), input(DR, DC, _),
    n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
    R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC.

:- input(BR, BC, V), V != 0,

   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),

   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != TileColor.

% Zero block: every sub-cell must be 0
:- input(BR, BC, 0),
   input(DR, DC, _),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,

% Grid boundary coordinates
min_row(R) :- R = #min{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
max_row(R) :- R = #max{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.

max_col(C) :- C = #max{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.

% 4-connected adjacency offsets
delta(0,1). delta(0,-1). delta(1,0). delta(-1,0).

% Non-3 cells on the grid boundary are reachable from outside
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_row(Rmin), R = Rmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_row(Rmax), R = Rmax.

outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_col(Cmax), C = Cmax.

% Flood-fill outward through non-3 cells
outside(R2, C2) :-
    outside(R1, C1), delta(DR, DC),
    R2 = R1+DR, C2 = C1+DC,

% Outside non-3 cells stay 0
:- outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 0.

% Interior non-3 cells (enclosed by 3s, not reachable from boundary) become 4
:- input(R, C, 0), not outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 4.

    non_wall(R1,C1).

reachable(R1,C1,R2,C2) :-
    reachable(R1,C1,R1,C1),            % reflexive
    neighbor(R1,C1,R2,C2).

higher_exists(R,C,Max) :-

output_cell(R,C) :- input(R,C,_).

wall(R,C) :- input(R,C,5).

neighbor(R1,C1,R2,C2) :-

%-------------------------------------------------
%  ARC-AGI – colour 5 walls
%  Each 4‑connected component of non‑wall cells (colour ≠5) is
%  filled with (max colour in that component + 5).

%-------------------------------------------------

% colour 5 acts as the wall
wall(R,C) :- input(R,C,5).

% non‑wall cells
non_wall(R,C) :- not wall(R,C).   % all cells except colour 5

delta(0,1).  delta(0,-1).  delta(1,0).  delta(-1,0).

% neighbour through non‑wall cells
neighbor(R1,C1,R2,C2) :-
    delta(DR,DC),
    R2 = R1 + DR,
    C2 = C1 + DC,
    R2 >= 0,  C2 >= 0,
    input(R2,C2,_),
    not wall(R2,C2),
    non_wall(R1,C1).

% 4‑connected reachability through non‑wall cells
reachable(R1,C1,R2,C2) :-
    reachable(R1,C1,R1,C1),            % reflexive
    neighbor(R1,C1,R2,C2).

reachable(R1,C1,R1,C1) :- true.

% does a strictly higher colour exist in the component?
higher_exists(R,C,Max) :-
    Color1 > Max,
    Color1 <= 9,
    Color1 != 5,
    reachable(R,C,R2,C2),

component_max(R,C,Max) :-

    Max != 5,
    not higher_exists(R,C,Max).

output(R,C,0) :- non_wall(R,C), component_max(R,C,0), color(0).

% every cell must have exactly one output colour
output_cell(R,C) :- input(R,C,_).

1 { output(R,C,Col) : color(Col) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).

cell(R,C) :- input(R,C,_).

wall(R,C) :- input(R,C,5).

    R2 = R1 + DR,
    C2 = C1 + DC,
    cell(R1,C1),               % source cell exists
    cell(R2,C2),               % target cell exists
    not wall(R1,C1),
    not wall(R2,C2).

% Reachability through non‑wall cells (transitive closure)
% Base case: a cell reaches itself
reachable(R,C,R,C) :- cell(R,C), path(R,C,R,C).

% Alternative: reachable from R to R2 via path

% Define whether a higher colour than Col exists reachable from (R,C)
higher_exists(R,C,Col) :-
    reachable(R,C,R2,C2),
    input(R2,C2,ColHigher),
    ColHigher > Col,
    ColHigher != 5.

% Max colour in component (excluding walls) – the greatest colour for which
% no higher colour is reachable.
component_max(R,C,Max) :-
    not wall(R,C),
    reachable(R,C,R2,C2),
    input(R2,C2,Max),
    Max != 5,
    not higher_exists(R,C,Max).

% Output for wall cells (colour 5 stays 5)
output(R,C,5) :- wall(R,C).

% Output for non‑wall cells: max+5 (must stay within 0‑9)
output(R,C,Out) :-
    not wall(R,C),
    component_max(R,C,Max),
    Max != 5,
    Out = Max + 5,
    Out <= 9,
    Out >= 5.

% Every cell must appear in the output
output_cell(R,C) :- cell(R,C).

% Exactly one answer set (one output per cell)
1 { output(R,C,Color) : color(Col) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).

% Colour domain
color(0..9).

%-------------------------------------------------
%  ARC-AGI – colour 5 walls
%  Each 4‑connected component of non‑wall cells (colour ≠5) is
%  filled with (max colour in that component + 5).
%  Cells that are colour 5 stay 5.
%-------------------------------------------------

% colour 5 acts as the wall
wall(R,C) :- input(R,C,5).

% non‑wall cells
non_wall(R,C) :- not wall(R,C).   % all cells except colour 5

% 4‑neighbour offsets
delta(0,1).  delta(0,-1).  delta(1,0).  delta(-1,0).

% neighbour through non‑wall cells
neighbor(R1,C1,R2,C2) :-
    delta(DR,DC),
    R2 = R1 + DR,
    C2 = C1 + DC,
    R2 >= 0,  C2 >= 0,
    input(R2,C2,_),
    not wall(R2,C2),
    non_wall(R1,C1).

% 4‑connected reachability through non‑wall cells
reachable(R1,C1,R2,C2) :-
    reachable(R1,C1,R1,C1),            % reflexive
    neighbor(R1,C1,R2,C2).

reachable(R1,C1,R1,C1) :- true.

% does a strictly higher colour exist in the component?
higher_exists(R,C,Max) :-
    Color1 > Max,
    Color1 <= 9,
    Color1 != 5,
    reachable(R,C,R2,C2),
    input(R2,C2,Color1).

% maximum colour of the component (the highest colour reachable)
component_max(R,C,Max) :-
    non_wall(R,C),
    reachable(R,C,R2,C2),
    input(R2,C2,Max),
    Max != 5,
    not higher_exists(R,C,Max).

% output for walls (colour 5 stays 5)
output(R,C,5) :- wall(R,C).

% output for a component whose maximal colour is > 0
output(R,C,6) :- non_wall(R,C), component_max(R,C,1), color(6).
output(R,C,7) :- non_wall(R,C), component_max(R,C,2), color(7).
output(R,C,8) :- non_wall(R,C), component_max(R,C,3), color(8).
output(R,C,9) :- non_wall(R,C), component_max(R,C,4), color(9).
% output for a component whose maximal colour is 0 (all‑zero component)
output(R,C,0) :- non_wall(R,C), component_max(R,C,0), color(0).

% every cell must have exactly one output colour
output_cell(R,C) :- input(R,C,_).

% exactly one answer set (one output per cell)
1 { output(R,C,Col) : color(Col) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).

% colour domain
color(0..9).
